published_statement: Ford-Roman gr-qc/9607003 p.2 Eq.(1) (verbatim via prior-stage read): 'for the free quantized massless scalar field in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, rho-hat == (t0/pi) INT <T00> dt/(t^2+t0^2) >= -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4), for all choices of the sampling time, t0. Here <T00> is the renormalized expectation value of the energy density evaluated in an arbitrary quantum state |psi>, in the frame of an arbitrary inertial observer'; EM field Eq.(48): -3/(16 pi^2 t0^4). LIGO (search-snippet summaries, NOT read): Tse et al. 2019 -- 'squeezed states improved the sensitivity of the LIGO interferometers to signals above 50 Hz by up to 3 dB, thereby increasing the expected detection rate by 40% (H1) and 50% (L1)'; Ganapathy et al. 2023 -- 'squeezing reduced the detector noise amplitude by a factor of 1.6 (4.0 dB) near 1 kHz' (Hanford) and 'a factor of 1.9 (5.8 dB)' (Livingston). The measured quantity in every case is quantum (shot / radiation-pressure) NOISE in the readout quadrature below the unsqueezed (vacuum) level -- not an energy density.
published_hypotheses: FR-H1 free (non-interacting) quantized field, minimal coupling (scalar); Maxwell field for Eq.(48)

FR-H3 four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, NO boundaries ('derived for Minkowski spacetime, in the absence of boundaries', p.2); extension to boundaries ARGUED (ref.[23]) for t0 much smaller than the distance to any boundary, not proved there
FR-H4 the bounded quantity is a Lorentzian TIME average of <T00> along an inertial worldline at ONE spatial point
FR-H6 arbitrary Fock-space state, <T00> normal ordered w.r.t. the Minkowski vacuum -- squeezed states included (the prior stage's 21,900 random multimode squeezed-state check; C1-C2 here)

LIGO-H1 (snippet-level) squeezed vacuum generated by an optical parametric oscillator (nonlinear crystal in a cavity) and injected at the dark port; the figure of merit is noise reduction in dB relative to no squeezing, in the detection band (tens of Hz to several kHz)

SQ-H1 (the identification that makes 'negative energy density' a statement about a measurement, computed here) single travelling linearly polarised plane-wave mode (or narrowband idealisation), energy density normal ordered w.r.t. the Minkowski vacuum; then Var(X_theta) below vacuum <=> <:E^2:> = <:T00:> < 0 at the times omega t = theta mod pi
hypothesis_drift: achievable.py:32 (and :28-29 heading 'THE CENSUS OF KNOWN NEGATIVE ENERGY DENSITY -- Everything real') -- STATUS WORD WIDENED: 'MEASURED' is attached to negative energy density. What LIGO (and every squeezing experiment) measures is a quadrature variance below the vacuum level. That is EXACTLY <:X_theta^2:> < 0 for any state with <X> = 0, pure or lossy (rederive A1-A3), and becomes <:T00:> < 0 only through the single-mode plane-wave identification SQ-H1 (B1). The negativity of T00 is therefore INFERRED from a measured quantity through a named idealisation, not measured as T00; the tree drops SQ-H1.

achievable.py:32 '(LIGO uses it)' -- DROPPED TIME-RESOLUTION HYPOTHESIS: the sign of the lab-frame energy density depends on the sampling time. At 1064 nm the Lorentzian-averaged rho-hat is negative only for t0 < t0* = -ln(tanh r)/(2 omega): 3.1e-16 s at 3 dB, 1.5e-16 s at 5.8 dB (D1), below the 3.5e-15 s optical period. At any time resolution LIGO's readout has (audio band, t0 = 3e-5 to 1.6e-2 s) the averaged energy density is +K sinh^2 r > 0 (E1). LIGO uses squeezed vacuum as a noise-reduction resource; it does not observe negative energy density, and nothing in the tree says it does so explicitly -- but the parenthesis is offered as the support for 'MEASURED'.

achievable.py:32 'Ford-Roman bounded' -- HYPOTHESES DROPPED SILENTLY: FR-H1 (free field), FR-H3 (Minkowski, no boundaries), FR-H4 (worldline time average). LIGO's squeezed field is generated inside a nonlinear crystal in an OPO cavity and stored in the arm cavities -- media and boundaries, where Eq.(1)/(48) is ARGUED (for t0 << boundary distance), not proved in the source. The drop is benign in practice (t0* c ~ 0.1 micron, far below every mirror spacing, so the argued regime is the relevant one), but it is a hypothesis, and it is unnamed. The EM coefficient is Eq.(48)'s 3/(16 pi^2), twice the scalar's.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (16 checks; output in rederive/squeezed-vacuum-ligo.out). A1 <:X_theta^2:> = sinh^2 r - sinh r cosh r cos(2 theta - phi) (sympy from <a^dag a>, <aa>). A2 min Var = e^{-2r}/2. A3 loss eta scales <:X^2:> by eta, sign kept -- so observed sub-vacuum noise is exactly <:X^2:> < 0 at the detector even for a mixed state. B1 plane-wave single mode: <:T00:> < 0 at phase theta <=> Var(X_theta) below vacuum. B2 negative fraction of each cycle arccos(tanh r)/pi < 1/2. C1 EXACT: min over r of the single-mode Lorentzian average [s^2 - q s sqrt(1+s^2)] = -(1 - sqrt(1-q^2))/2, q = e^{-2 omega t0}; C2 this is >= Ford-Roman's finite-V bound -q/2 on all q in [0,1] (sqrt(1-q^2) >= 1-q), equality only at q in {0,1} -- the squeezed vacuum is Ford-Roman bounded, approaching and never crossing. D1 negativity survives averaging only for t0 < t0*: 3.112e-16 s (3 dB), 2.380e-16 s (4.0 dB), 1.521e-16 s (5.8 dB), 1.787e-17 s (15 dB) at 1064 nm; optical period 3.549e-15 s. E1 at LIGO's band (10 Hz - 5 kHz) q underflows to 0 and rho-hat = +K sinh^2 r > 0. F1 over a NAMED generous box (3-15 dB; squeezed bandwidth 1e4-1e9 Hz; beam area 1e-8 to 1e-4 m^2; narrowband energy scale K = hbar omega dnu/(c A)), the largest |negative rho-hat| is 1e-13 of FR's EM bound at the same t0. lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for THIS result. The Ford-Roman bound (1995-97) takes no measured input: it is a theorem about the free field, so no later datum can move it. What its authors had was squeezed light at a few dB (Wu-Kimble-Hall-Wu 1986, cited p.2). What came later: ~15 dB laboratory squeezing (2016), LIGO's operational squeezing (2019, 3 dB; 2023, 4.0/5.8 dB), and direct subcycle time-domain sampling of squeezed vacuum (Riek et al. 2015-2017). Evidence that the new data do NOT change the conclusion: (1) stronger squeezing only deepens the single-mode dip toward its floor, and the exact minimum -(1-sqrt(1-q^2))/2 never crosses the FR finite-V bound -q/2 (C1-C2); (2) at every sampling time where the negativity survives averaging (t0 < ~3e-16 s) the laboratory magnitude sits >= 13 orders below the EM bound (F1), so no realistic beam comes near testing it. Evidence the other way, stated so it is not presumed away: Maclay & Davis (2019) read published OPA / homodyne data as violating 'a proposed QI for squeezed light' -- the one place where data are claimed against a QI. Not read here; its target inequality and identification are unknown, and the computation (E1) shows homodyne-band sampling yields positive lab-frame rho-hat, so the natural reading does not reach FR Eq.(1). It stays CONTESTED. What the data did change is the tree's word, not the physics: later data make it clearer that what is measured (LIGO) is sub-vacuum quadrature noise, and that negative energy density itself is resolved, if at all, only in subcycle time-domain experiments, not in LIGO.
grade_evidence: Two of the three clauses stand; the third holds on a smaller class than the tree states. (1) 'Ford-Roman bounded' STANDS for the free field in Minkowski space: exact single-mode minimum -(1-sqrt(1-q^2))/2 >= FR finite-V bound -q/2 (C1-C2, sympy), consistent with the prior stage's at-source read and its 21,900-state multimode check; the bound is non-binding by >= 13 orders for laboratory squeezed light (F1). The tree drops FR-H1/H3/H4 unnamed, and LIGO's squeezed field lives in crystal and cavities where the bound is argued, not proved (benign: t0* c ~ 0.1 um). (2) 'LIGO uses it' is corroborated by search summaries of Tse 2019 and Ganapathy 2023 only -- NOT read at source this stage. (3) 'MEASURED' as NEGATIVE ENERGY DENSITY is NARROWED: the measured quantity is sub-vacuum quadrature variance, which is exactly <:X_theta^2:> < 0 (A1-A3) and is <:T00:> < 0 only through the single-mode plane-wave identification (B1), on a sub-half fraction of each optical cycle (B2), surviving time-averaging only for t0 < 3.1e-16 s at 3 dB (D1); at LIGO's readout resolution the averaged lab-frame energy density is POSITIVE (E1). LIGO measures the squeezing; the negative energy density is inferred. Nothing here is WRONG, and the narrowing does not move what rests on it: the census row still names a real, laboratory-made state with negative <:T00:> that obeys a QEI, and the SURVEY verdict 'core not buildable with known physics' (achievable.py:25-26, 149) is untouched (if anything reinforced by F1). Discrepancy recorded, not repaired: paper/CLAIMS.md:665-673 still carries the census under the DOCKET-55-withdrawn spatial-cap sentence. One CONTESTED item (Maclay-Davis 2019) is NAMED-NOT-READ and not adjudicated. Limitation of this audit, stated: no source page was opened this stage (alphaXiv quota exhausted, egress blocked); FR is used via a prior stage's at-source read, the LIGO/Riek/Maclay-Davis clauses via search summaries, and every load-bearing step of the grade is COMPUTED.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owner names the identification (single-mode plane wave, Minkowski-normal-ordered) and the time resolution (sub-cycle) behind 'MEASURED', or cites a measurement that resolves the negative window (e.g. Riek et al. 2017, once read at source), and names FR-H1/H3/H4 on 'Ford-Roman bounded'. To OPEN: if reading Tse 2019 / Ganapathy 2023 at source contradicted the snippet-level claim that LIGO operates with injected squeezed vacuum (not expected, but it is snippet-only here). To WRONG (for the 'Ford-Roman bounded' clause): a squeezed state of the free EM field in Minkowski space with Lorentzian-averaged rho-hat < -3/(16 pi^2 t0^4) -- excluded by C1-C2 for a single mode and by the prior stage's multimode check -- or, for the laboratory field, Maclay-Davis's violation shown on reading to be of FR Eq.(1)/(48) itself with a correct identification; that would bear on FR-H1/H3 (media, cavities) rather than on the Minkowski theorem. To DATA-DEPENDENT: none foreseeable -- no datum enters either the identity A1-B1 or the theorem.
